label: Friends turned ideological rivals
summary: The founding conflict of the X-Men. They met as young men in Israel (shown in flashback in Uncanny X-Men #161, 1982), bonded over being mutants, and split over whether coexistence with humans was possible. Every subsequent decade restages the argument; the Krakoan era finally put them on the same council.

events.note: Magneto attacks Cape Citadel; the X-Men's first mission is against Xavier's old friend.
Flashback: Charles and Erik meet in Haifa, fight Baron Strucker together, and part over ideology.
Xavier, dying, hands Magneto the school and the New Mutants.
Fatal Attractions prelude; Magneto returns to Asteroid M and dies (apparently) in the fall.
Xavier and Magneto co-found the mutant nation of Krakoa.

label: First love, marriage, Phoenix, death
summary: The franchise's central romance. A shy mutual crush in 1963 became the marriage in X-Men #30 (1994), was broken by Jean's death as Dark Phoenix, by her resurrection, by Scott's psychic affair with Emma Frost, and by Jean's second death. Her Krakoan return left them cordial co-workers rather than a couple.

events.note: Scott's unspoken feelings for Jean are established in the first issue.
Dark Phoenix Saga ends with Jean's suicide on the Moon to stop herself.
Scott and Jean marry.
Jean discovers Scott's psychic affair with Emma.
Jean is killed by Xorn/Magneto; she tells Scott to live.

label: Rivals for Jean, then for the X-Men
summary: Started as a love-triangle rivalry over Jean Grey and became a philosophical one: Logan, the soldier, came to believe children should be kept out of the war; Scott, the field leader, came to believe there was no one else to fight it. The 2011 Schism split the X-Men between them.

events.note: Logan joins; friction with Cyclops's leadership is immediate.
Wolverine's famous 'Now it's my turn' in the Hellfire Club, while Scott is captured.
The two fight on Utopia over whether to send students into battle; Wolverine leaves to reopen the school.
Logan sides with the Avengers against a Phoenix-possessed Cyclops.

label: Unrequited, mostly
summary: Logan's attraction to Jean is written as intense and almost never acted on; Jean's response varies by writer from fond refusal to genuine temptation. The relationship is largely about restraint, and it is consummated only in alternate futures.

events.note: Logan's interest in Jean is first made explicit.
Stranded on Asteroid M, Jean and Logan kiss; Logan kills her so the Phoenix will take over and save them.
Phoenix-Jean seeks out Logan; he refuses her repeatedly.

label: Psychic affair to power couple
summary: Began as telepathic 'therapy' during Scott's marriage, became an affair, and after Jean's death became the X-Men's leadership couple through the Utopia era. Ended when Phoenix-possessed Scott turned on Emma; they have remained allies with history since.

events.note: Emma offers Scott telepathic counselling; it turns intimate.
Jean, from the future, pushes Scott toward Emma; they kiss on Jean's grave and reopen the school.
Headmaster and headmistress; the relationship becomes the team's centre.
Scott takes Emma's share of the Phoenix by force.

label: Rivals who respect each other
summary: A rivalry with uncommon mutual respect. Jean's psychic confrontation with Emma in New X-Men #139 is the high point; by the Krakoan era they are colleagues who occasionally still needle each other about Scott.

events.note: Jean tears through Emma's mind after discovering the affair.

events.issue: Phoenix Resurrection: The Return of Jean Grey #5 (2018)
events.note: Jean's return; Emma among those present.

label: Closest confidants, briefly lovers
summary: The two most senior members of the 1975 team, each the other's most trusted colleague. Written as a near-sibling friendship for decades, with a romantic period during Jason Aaron's Wolverine and the X-Men (2012–2014) that the line has mostly treated as a chapter rather than a change.

events.note: Storm takes over as team leader with Logan's backing.
Storm and Logan begin a relationship.
Logan dies; Storm leads the mourning.

label: Big sister, then peer
summary: Storm was the first adult X-Man Kitty bonded with; the relationship strained when Storm's punk-era change (Uncanny X-Men #173) frightened her, and matured into equals by the time Kitty led the team.

events.note: Storm recruits Kitty in Deerfield, Illinois.
Kitty rejects Storm's new look and the two fall out.
Reconciliation.

label: Decades on and off
summary: A teenage crush that became a long, intermittently written romance. Broken off in Secret Wars (1985) when Piotr fell for an alien healer; revived in Astonishing X-Men; nearly ended in marriage in X-Men Gold #30 (2018), when Kitty called it off at the altar.

events.note: Kitty, 13, is immediately smitten with Piotr.
Piotr falls for Zsaji on Battleworld; the relationship ends.
Colossus returns from apparent death; the romance restarts.
Kitty halts the wedding; Rogue and Gambit marry instead.

label: Brother and sister
summary: Piotr's protectiveness and Illyana's transformation into a demon sorceress define the relationship; he keeps trying to see the child she was, and she keeps refusing to be seen that way. Her death in the Legacy Virus storyline (Uncanny X-Men #303, 1993) and later return is one of his central griefs.

events.note: Illyana is taken to Limbo and returns moments later aged seven years.
Illyana dies of the Legacy Virus.
Magik, restored, rejoins the team.

label: From fear to family
summary: Kitty initially recoiled from Kurt's appearance; Claremont used her growing affection for him as the story of the reader learning to see past surfaces. They are close for the rest of the run.

events.note: Kitty is frightened by Nightcrawler on first meeting.
Christmas issue: Kitty alone at the mansion, Kurt among those she now counts as family.

label: Best friends; the devil and the saint
summary: The franchise's most consistently written male friendship. Kurt is the one person Logan does not perform for; Kurt's death in X-Force vol. 3 #26 (2010) broke Logan, and his return on Krakoa restored the pairing.

events.note: Early baseball-game issue establishing the team's off-duty bonds.
Nightcrawler dies saving Hope Summers; Logan carries the grief for years.
Kurt returns from the afterlife.

label: Mother who abandoned him
summary: Hinted at since Uncanny X-Men #142 (1981) and confirmed in 1994: Mystique bore Kurt and, fleeing a mob, let him fall into a river. The relationship is about whether he can forgive her and whether she wants him to. Krakoa, where she sat on the Quiet Council while he served as its moral voice, kept the question open.

events.note: Mystique hints she knows Nightcrawler's parentage.
Mystique confirms she is Kurt's mother.
'The Draco' names Azazel as his father.

label: Foster mother and daughter
summary: Mystique and Destiny raised Rogue after her powers manifested, then used her as a Brotherhood weapon. Rogue's defection to the X-Men was a betrayal from Mystique's side and an escape from Rogue's; the two have spent decades alternating between manipulation and genuine care.

events.note: Rogue debuts as Mystique's protégé, absorbing Ms. Marvel's powers permanently.
Rogue asks Xavier for help and joins the X-Men.
Rogue gains control of her power; Mystique's manipulations in the surrounding arc resurface.

label: The 90s' great slow burn
summary: A romance built on Rogue being unable to touch anyone and Gambit being unable to be honest with anyone. Spanned betrayals (his Marauders past, the Antarctica abandonment in Uncanny X-Men #350), separations, and the 2018 wedding; still married on Krakoa and after.

events.note: Their flirtation begins in earnest.
Rogue abandons Gambit in Antarctica after his Mutant Massacre role is revealed.
Rogue and Gambit marry.

label: Savage Land interlude
summary: A brief, deliberate romance in the Savage Land that Claremont wrote as two outsiders recognising each other. It mattered mostly for what it set up: Rogue's enduring sympathy for Magneto and the alternate-universe marriage in the Age of Apocalypse.

events.note: Rogue and Magneto, depowered and stranded, become close.
Magneto executes Zaladane; Rogue cannot follow him.

label: Married, with a son
summary: In the Age of Apocalypse, where Xavier died before founding the X-Men, Magneto leads the team and is married to Rogue; their son is Charles. The pairing is the clearest example of the database's premise: the same two characters, a different continuity, a different relationship.

events.note: Magneto and Rogue shown as husband and wife.

label: Favourite son to patricide
summary: Xavier's first and most loyal student. The relationship curdled as Scott learned how much Xavier had hidden (Deadly Genesis, 2006), and ended when a Phoenix-possessed Scott killed Xavier. Krakoa, with Xavier resurrected, treated it as a wound neither wanted to discuss.

events.note: Scott is Xavier's field leader from the first mission.
Scott learns Xavier erased his memory of a lost team and expels him from the mansion.
Dark Phoenix Cyclops kills Xavier.

label: Mentor, with a buried complication
summary: Xavier trained Jean's telepathy from childhood. X-Men #3 (1964) briefly gave him secret romantic feelings for her, a thread later writers abandoned and then treated as evidence of his ethical blind spots.

events.note: A thought balloon reveals Xavier's attraction to Jean; it is never pursued.
Jean's Phoenix return; Xavier's role in suppressing her power earlier is part of the backstory.

label: Teacher, then colleague
summary: Logan trained Kitty in Japan after her kidnapping by Ogun; she is the first of his series of young protégées (later Jubilee, Armor, Laura). As an adult she ran his school after his death.

events.note: Logan rescues and retrains Kitty in Japan; she takes the name Shadowcat.
Kitty is co-headmistress of the Jean Grey School.

label: Mutual contempt, grudging respect
summary: Kitty never forgave Emma's Hellfire Club past; Whedon's Astonishing X-Men built the team's internal tension on Kitty's suspicion that Emma had not changed. Emma's later rescue of Kitty from the bullet (Uncanny X-Men #522, 2010) did not fully close the account.

events.note: Kitty is recruited specifically to keep an eye on Emma.
Emma, under the Hellfire Club's influence, turns on Kitty.

label: Lifelong partners
summary: Claremont wrote them as a couple from Destiny's first appearance, in code, because editorial would not allow it to be stated. Destiny's death in Uncanny X-Men #255 (1990) drove Mystique's choices for decades; her Krakoan resurrection, which Mystique forced, is the spine of Inferno (2021) and Immortal X-Men.

events.note: Destiny debuts with the Brotherhood alongside Mystique.
Destiny is killed by Legion.
Destiny is resurrected; the two are stated on the page as married.

label: Oldest friends in the franchise
summary: The two original X-Men who most often left and returned together (the Champions, the Defenders, X-Factor). Bobby came out to Hank in All-New X-Men #40 (2015) among the first to know; the Krakoan era's divergence, with Hank running X-Force's dirty work, strained but did not break it.

events.note: Both among the original five.
Both leave the X-Men to form the Champions.
Young Bobby comes out; adult Bobby follows in Uncanny X-Men #600.

label: Brothers, perpetually compared
summary: Separated as children after a plane crash, reunited as adults. Alex has spent most of his career defining himself against Scott—leading X-Factor and the Avengers Unity Squad as the brother who is not Cyclops—and the two have fought on opposite sides more than once.

events.note: Alex is introduced and revealed as Scott's brother.
Alex leads the Unity Squad while Scott is imprisoned.

label: The team's two matriarchs
summary: Close from the start of the new team; Storm was Jean's closest female friend through the Phoenix years and held the team together in her absences.

events.note: Jean becomes Phoenix; Storm is at her side.
Returned Jean recruits Storm first for her new team.

label: Teenage version
summary: In the Ultimate universe they are teenagers, the romance is more volatile, and Jean briefly chooses Wolverine. Included as a continuity contrast to the 616 marriage.

events.note: Scott and Jean established as a couple at Xavier's.
Jean leaves Scott for Logan, briefly.

label: Student who became the professor's peer
summary: Hank was the original X-Man most like Xavier intellectually, and the one who most often argued with him as an equal. On Krakoa their relationship inverted: Beast ran the operations Xavier would not look at directly.

events.note: Among the original five students.
Beast takes charge of Krakoa's intelligence arm with Xavier's tacit blessing.

label: The youngest student
summary: Bobby was the youngest of the first class and the one Xavier treated most as a child; later writers used that to explain how long it took anyone to notice the scale of his power.

events.note: Joins as the youngest of the original five.

label: Original teammates, later at odds
summary: Teammates for sixty years whose friendship cracked when Hank refused to follow Scott into militancy on Utopia (Uncanny X-Men #519–520, 2010) and then brought the time-displaced original X-Men to the present to shame him (All-New X-Men #1, 2012).

events.note: Original teammates.
Beast pulls the young X-Men from the past to confront the adult Cyclops.

label: The leader and the class clown
summary: Bobby spent the Silver Age needling Scott's seriousness and the modern era following him anyway; he was on Scott's side of the Schism.

events.note: Original teammates.
Iceman stays with Cyclops on Utopia.

label: Closest of the original five
summary: Hank and Jean were the two originals who stayed closest; he was the scientist she trusted with the Phoenix question, and her deaths hit him hardest after Scott's.

events.note: Reunited in X-Factor after Jean's return.

label: Teammates; she outed him before he did
summary: The time-displaced young Jean read Bobby's mind and told him he was gay in All-New X-Men #40 (2015), a scene that was criticised for her lack of consent and celebrated for what it did for the character.

events.note: Young Jean tells young Bobby what she has read in his mind.

label: The scientist and the soldier
summary: Rarely hostile, often sharp: two of the team's most senior members who disagree about means. Their Krakoan-era X-Force partnership, in which Beast became the more ruthless of the two, inverted the dynamic.

events.note: Both on Krakoa's X-Force; Beast's ethics drift past Wolverine's.

label: The marriage Marvel undid
summary: 'Face it, tiger, you just hit the jackpot.' From that first line to the wedding in Amazing Spider-Man Annual #21 (1987) to the deal with Mephisto in One More Day (2007) that erased the marriage from everyone's memory. They have been on and off ever since; the relationship is the clearest example of editorial intervening in a dynamic.

events.note: MJ's face is finally shown.
MJ reveals she has always known Peter is Spider-Man.
The wedding.
One More Day: the marriage is erased.

label: First love, ended on a bridge
summary: Peter's college girlfriend and the great tragedy of the book. Her death at the Green Goblin's hands — with Peter's own web-line possibly snapping her neck — is the moment the series stopped being a Silver Age comic.

events.note: Gwen introduced at Empire State University.
The Night Gwen Stacy Died.

label: Best friend who became the Goblin
summary: Roommates at ESU; Harry's drug addiction (ASM #96–98, the issues that broke the Comics Code), his discovery of Peter's identity, and his turn as the second Green Goblin. He died saving Peter in Spectacular Spider-Man #200 (1993) and was later restored by One More Day.

events.note: Harry's drug storyline, published without Code approval.
Harry becomes the Green Goblin.
Harry dies saving Peter and Normie.

label: Archenemy who knows his name
summary: The only Spider-Man villain whose enmity is fully personal: Norman learned Peter's identity in ASM #39 (1966), killed Gwen in #121, apparently died in #122, and returned in 1996 to orchestrate the Clone Saga. Every major Spider-Man storyline about loss runs through him.

events.note: Osborn unmasked as the Goblin; learns Peter's identity.
Goblin impaled on his own glider.
Norman revealed alive, behind the Clone Saga.

label: Son who could never satisfy him
summary: Norman's contempt for Harry is the origin of nearly everything wrong with Harry; the Goblin identity passed from father to son as a kind of inheritance.

events.note: Norman's origin reveals his coldness toward Harry.

label: The reason for the mask
summary: For four decades the book's central secret existed to protect her. When she finally learned the truth — Amazing Spider-Man vol. 2 #38 (2002), in a single conversation — it was one of the best-regarded issues of the era.

events.note: Uncle Ben dies; May becomes Peter's responsibility.
'The Conversation': May tells Peter she knows.

label: She wanted Spider-Man, not Peter
summary: Felicia fell for the mask and was openly disappointed by the man under it — the inverse of the MJ relationship. Partners, lovers and occasional opponents for forty years; the pairing was written as adults, which made it unusual for the book.

events.note: Black Cat debuts.
Peter unmasks; Felicia is unimpressed by Peter Parker.

label: The rejected suit and the ruined man
summary: Eddie Brock blamed Spider-Man for his career; the symbiote blamed him for rejection. Together they were the first villain who knew Peter's identity and could evade his spider-sense. The enmity has softened since Venom became an anti-hero.

events.note: Venom debuts, menacing Mary Jane.
Truce: Venom becomes an anti-hero.

label: Rival who lived in his body
summary: Otto was the first villain to beat Spider-Man and, fifty years later, the one who replaced him: dying, he swapped minds with Peter and ran as the Superior Spider-Man for thirty-one issues. No other rivalry at Marvel has that shape.

events.note: Doc Ock defeats Spider-Man in his first appearance.
Otto takes over Peter's body.
Otto yields the body back to Peter.

label: Two Spider-Men
summary: Peter first met Miles across universes in Spider-Men (2012); after Secret Wars moved Miles to 616 they shared New York, and Peter became the mentor he never had.

events.note: Peter crosses into the Ultimate universe and meets Miles.
Miles operating in Earth-616.

label: Successor to a dead Peter
summary: In the Ultimate universe Miles took the name after Peter Parker died (Ultimate Spider-Man #160); the two met only briefly when a resurrected Ultimate Peter returned. A different relationship from the 616 one: inheritance, not mentorship.

events.note: Ultimate Peter Parker dies.
Miles debuts.

label: Rivals written as friends
summary: Introduced as competing love interests, they were mostly friends on the page; MJ's silent presence at Peter's apartment after Gwen's death (ASM #122) is the panel that turned her from party girl into the series' adult.

events.note: MJ stays with Peter the night after Gwen dies.

label: Avengers teammates who annoy each other
summary: A 1987 one-shot in which Logan's world got a civilian killed set the tone; New Avengers (2005–2012) made them teammates and the odd-couple friendship became one of Bendis's recurring jokes.

events.note: Peter accidentally kills Logan's old flame Charlie.
Both founding members of the New Avengers.

label: Ultimate universe teenage romance
summary: In the Ultimate universe, Peter and Kitty dated briefly between his breakups with MJ — a pairing with no 616 equivalent, and a good example of what a continuity filter is for.

events.note: Peter and Kitty begin dating.
Kitty ends it; Peter returns to MJ.
